facts.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating/Cu matrix system was studied by simulated nanoindentation and friction testing at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K.
A virtual indenter was driven at 10 m/s to a maximum indentation depth of 30 Å.
The loading stage lasted 300 ps, followed by 300 ps of unloading at the same indenter speed.
The simulations used periodic boundaries in X and Y and a contractive boundary in Z.
The bulk was evolved in an NVE ensemble, while a constant-temperature layer was controlled with a Langevin thermostat.
At 300–600 K, the lattice remained ordered and the dislocation density was comparatively stable.
At 900–1200 K, rapid lattice disorder was accompanied by a significant reduction in dislocation density.
Above 900 K, deformation shifted from stacking-fault-mediated behavior toward lattice-disorder-mediated behavior.
The fraction of HCP-coordinated atoms increased with temperature.
Hardness and wear resistance remained relatively stable through 600 K but decreased sharply at and above 900 K relative to 300 K.
Hardness was about 17.4 GPa at 300–600 K, 10.2 GPa at 900 K, and 8.6 GPa at 1200 K.
The friction coefficient and tangential force increased with temperature and showed strong fluctuations above 900 K.
